channel.title: The AI Chronicle
channel.description: Daily AI news — India focus and global mix

item.title: Tencent Commits $100 Million to India's Gaming and Animation Sector Through SEPC and GDAI Partnerships
item.description: Chinese tech giant Tencent has announced a $100 million investment in India's gaming and animation industry through strategic partnerships with the Software Export Promotion Council and the Game Developers Association of India. The investment aims to nurture local developer talent, fund studios and help Indian gaming content reach global audiences. The commitment aligns with India's ambitions to grow its Animation, Visual Effects, Gaming and Comics sector into a significant export industry.

item.title: Shadowfax Plans 100 New Dark Stores in FY27 as It Bets on Quick Commerce for Next Growth Phase
item.description: Logistics startup Shadowfax has announced plans to open 100 dark stores across India in FY27 as it pivots quick commerce into its primary growth engine. The expansion signals that third-party logistics players are moving up the value chain by owning fulfilment infrastructure rather than just providing delivery services. The push puts Shadowfax in more direct competition with Blinkit, Zepto, and Swiggy Instamart as the quick commerce market consolidates.

item.title: Numero AI Acquires Royu in Cash-and-Stock Deal to Build Agentic Finance Platform for Enterprises
item.description: Indian AI startup Numero AI has acquired Royu in a cash-and-stock transaction to accelerate the development of an agentic AI platform targeting the finance and controller functions of large enterprises. The combined entity aims to automate tasks currently performed manually by finance teams, including reconciliation, reporting and compliance workflows. The deal reflects growing investor and founder interest in deploying AI agents to replace repetitive back-office roles in Indian corporates.

item.title: AI Startups Face Lower Margins Than SaaS Era, Kalaari Capital Urges Founders to Prove Unit Economics
item.description: Kalaari Capital's Harshit Kumar has warned that AI-native startups in India face structurally lower gross margins than traditional SaaS companies due to rising inference costs and the expense of human review processes. He argues that Indian AI founders must prioritise building defensible moats and demonstrating measurable customer ROI rather than relying on growth metrics alone. The advice signals a maturing in investor expectations as the AI startup funding cycle moves from enthusiasm to scrutiny.

item.title: Dhruva Space Receives Rs 105 Crore From Government to Develop Flat-Pack Satellite Platform
item.description: Hyderabad-based space startup Dhruva Space has secured Rs 105 crore in government funding to develop a flat-pack satellite platform designed for efficient launch stacking, faster system integration, and large-scale constellation deployments. The flat-pack architecture is intended to reduce the cost and time required to build and launch multiple satellites, supporting India's growing ambitions in commercial space. The grant comes under India's broader push to build a self-reliant private space ecosystem.

item.title: Ola Electric Pumps Rs 2,000 Crore Into EV and Battery Manufacturing to Boost Localisation
item.description: Ola Electric Mobility has approved a Rs 2,000 crore capital infusion into its EV and battery cell manufacturing subsidiaries as part of a push to deepen localisation and vertical integration across its supply chain. The investment is aimed at strengthening the company's core two-wheeler EV business and scaling battery production at a time of intensifying competition from legacy players and new entrants. The move comes as Ola Electric faces profitability pressure and scrutiny over after-sales service quality.

item.title: Dainik Bhaskar and Indian Publishers File CCI Complaint Against Google Over AI Search Revenue Sharing
item.description: Dainik Bhaskar and a coalition of Indian media publishers have jointly filed a complaint with the Competition Commission of India against Google, alleging that AI-driven changes to search results are reducing traffic to news sites and cutting publisher advertising revenues without fair compensation. The publishers argue that Google's AI Overviews and related features extract news content to generate direct answers, diverting users away from publishers' websites. The CCI complaint follows similar actions by publishers in Europe and Australia and could set a precedent for how AI-generated search interacts with Indian media rights.

item.title: Flipkart Pauses IPO Plans Indefinitely Amid Rising Market Volatility and Crowded Public Issue Pipeline
item.description: Walmart-owned Flipkart has indefinitely paused its long-anticipated IPO discussions as rising market volatility and a congested public issue pipeline make the timing unfavourable. The company is instead redirecting investment into its quick commerce arm, Flipkart Minutes, as e-commerce growth shows signs of plateauing. The pause follows similar postponements by other major Indian tech firms and signals caution in the broader Indian startup IPO market.

item.title: Over 12 Lakh Indian Chemists Plan May 20 Shutdown Over Fake AI-Generated Prescriptions
item.description: More than 1.2 million chemists across India are planning a nationwide shop shutdown on May 20 in protest against e-pharmacies that are allegedly enabling the use of AI-generated fake prescriptions to fulfil medicine orders. The chemists argue that AI tools are being used to fabricate prescription documents, bypassing regulatory safeguards and endangering patient safety. The protest marks a flashpoint in the broader conflict between traditional pharmacy networks and digital medicine platforms.

item.title: Gig Workers Plan Nationwide 5-Hour Shutdown Over Rising Fuel Costs and Stagnant Per-KM Pay
item.description: A gig and platform workers' union has called a nationwide five-hour shutdown to protest rising fuel prices that are eroding take-home earnings for delivery and ride-hailing workers. The union is demanding an immediate upward revision of per-kilometre service rates, arguing that platforms have not adjusted pay to reflect input cost increases. The action could disrupt food delivery, cab and package services across Indian cities on the day of the protest.

item.title: AI Startup Margins Under Pressure: Kalaari Capital Says Indian AI Founders Must Prove Unit Economics, Not Just Growth
item.description: Kalaari Capital investor Harshit Kumar has publicly warned that AI-native startups in India cannot rely on the high gross margins that defined the SaaS era, as rising inference costs and the need for human review layers are structurally compressing profitability. Kumar advised founders to build measurable customer outcomes and defensible moats rather than competing on feature breadth. The commentary reflects a broader investor recalibration in India's AI startup ecosystem as the initial hype cycle gives way to scrutiny of sustainable business models.

item.title: ED Freezes Rs 526 Crore of Gameskraft Assets, Alleges AI Bots Manipulated Online Rummy Games
item.description: India's Enforcement Directorate has frozen Rs 526.49 crore in assets belonging to online gaming platform Gameskraft as part of a money laundering investigation, with authorities alleging the company deployed bots to manipulate outcomes in real-money rummy games. The ED further alleges Gameskraft operated in Indian states where real-money gaming is legally prohibited. The case marks one of the most significant regulatory enforcement actions against an Indian online gaming platform and raises questions about the use of automated agents in consumer-facing games.

item.title: Karnataka Fast-Tracks Drone Testing Facility Near Bengaluru to Lead India's Drone Economy
item.description: The Karnataka government is accelerating development of a dedicated drone testing facility near Bengaluru as part of its strategy to become the anchor state in India's rapidly growing drone economy. The facility is intended to provide a certified environment for drone manufacturers, startups, and defence-adjacent companies to test unmanned aerial systems without navigating the complexities of airspace permissions. Karnataka already hosts a significant concentration of drone and aerospace startups and is competing with states like Uttar Pradesh and Telangana for leadership in the sector.

item.title: Rapido Raises $240 Million Led by Prosus at $3 Billion Valuation as Indian Ride-Hailing Competition Intensifies
item.description: Bengaluru-based ride-hailing platform Rapido has raised $240 million in primary funding led by Prosus, valuing the company at $3 billion and making it one of India's most valuable mobility startups. The company plans to use the capital to strengthen its technology platform, expand its driver and rider network, and deepen its market presence against rivals Ola and Uber. The raise comes as Maharashtra's transport minister separately called for a shutdown of bike taxi services operated by Rapido, Ola, and Uber, creating a regulatory overhang.

item.title: Anthropic's Claude Now Writes Over 90% of Its Own Code, CFO Krishna Rao Reveals
item.description: Anthropic CFO Krishna Rao has disclosed that Claude, the company's flagship AI model, now generates more than 90% of Anthropic's internal codebase, a striking indicator of how AI is reshaping even the most AI-native workplaces. Despite this automation, Anthropic is continuing to hire, positioning AI as an amplifier of human talent rather than a replacement. The disclosure has immediate relevance for Indian software engineers and IT professionals who face growing pressure to justify their roles as AI coding tools mature.

item.title: OpenAI's India Head Pragya Misra Urges Indian Startups to Build for Future AI Problems, Not Just Today's
item.description: OpenAI's India policy and partnerships head Pragya Misra has cautioned Indian startups against 'recency bias' — building products that solve only today's AI limitations rather than anticipating capabilities that will exist within two to three years. She described India as one of OpenAI's most important testing grounds globally, given the country's scale and linguistic diversity. Misra also stressed that technical depth remains non-negotiable for founders even as AI tools lower the barrier to product creation.

item.title: Sarvam AI's Vivek Raghavan: 'Data in Motion' From Real Users Is the Most Valuable AI Asset for Indian Startups
item.description: Sarvam AI cofounder Vivek Raghavan has publicly argued that real-time user interaction data — what he calls 'data in motion' — is the single most valuable competitive asset for AI companies, surpassing static training datasets. Raghavan's perspective is particularly relevant for Indian startups building AI products for India's diverse, multilingual user base, where live usage patterns are difficult to replicate. Sarvam AI, which recently reached a $1.5 billion valuation, has built its own 105-billion-parameter model tailored to Indian languages.

item.title: Dainik Bhaskar and Indian Publishers File CCI Complaint Against Google Over AI Search Revenue Sharing
item.description: Dainik Bhaskar, one of India's largest Hindi-language media groups, has joined other publishers in filing a complaint with the Competition Commission of India against Google, citing concerns over unfair revenue sharing as AI-driven search reduces traffic to news websites. The publishers allege that Google's AI-powered search summaries are displaying their content without adequate compensation. This filing marks a significant escalation in the global publisher-versus-platform dispute, now formally entering India's competition regulatory arena.

item.title: India Releases First Funds Under Rs 1 Lakh Crore RDI Scheme, Backing Five Deep Tech Startups
item.description: The Indian government has disbursed the first cheques under its Rs 1 lakh crore Research, Development and Innovation Fund, selecting five deep tech startups working across space, robotics, batteries, drones, and advanced healthcare. This marks a significant milestone in India's push to translate state capital into frontier technology development. The RDI Scheme is one of the largest government-backed innovation funding mechanisms in India's history.

item.title: Over 12 Lakh Indian Chemists Plan May 20 Shutdown Over Fake AI-Generated Prescriptions
item.description: More than 1.2 million chemists across India are planning a nationwide shop shutdown on May 20 in protest against e-pharmacies allegedly accepting AI-generated fake prescriptions. The strike signals a deepening conflict between traditional pharmacy networks and online medicine platforms over patient safety and regulatory compliance. The dispute exposes a critical gap in India's health regulatory framework as AI tools become capable of producing convincing medical documentation.

item.title: Electric Two-Wheeler Makers in India Face Margin Squeeze as AI Infrastructure Boom Drives Up Chip Costs
item.description: India's electric two-wheeler manufacturers are facing significant margin pressure and potential retail price increases as raw material costs surge and global AI infrastructure demand intensifies competition for lithium-ion cells and memory chips. The AI data centre boom is creating upstream supply chain pressure that is now directly affecting the cost of affordable EVs for Indian commuters. Manufacturers warn that price hikes may be unavoidable unless government intervention stabilises input costs, with implications for India's EV adoption targets and the tens of millions of households considering a switch from petrol bikes.

item.title: HrdWyr Raises $13M Series A From Ideaspring Capital to Develop Fabless Semiconductor Chips in India
item.description: Bengaluru-based fabless semiconductor startup HrdWyr has raised $13 million in a Series A round led by Ideaspring Capital to fund product development and market expansion. The company designs chips without owning its own manufacturing facilities, a model that allows Indian startups to compete in semiconductor design while the country builds out its fabrication ecosystem. The funding comes as India pushes to build domestic chip design capacity alongside its semiconductor manufacturing ambitions, with HrdWyr representing an emerging cohort of deep-tech startups that could reduce India's dependence on foreign chip architectures.

item.title: Tamil Nadu Police Used IT Rules to Ask X to Block 18 URLs Belonging to Ruling Party's Critics
item.description: Tamil Nadu Police invoked Section 79(3)(b) of India's IT Act to request that X (formerly Twitter) block 18 URLs, which allegedly belong to DMK supporters who shared commentary criticising the Tamil Viduthalai Kazhagam party and the Chief Minister's office. The requests represent a pattern of state-level police agencies using federal IT law powers to suppress political speech online, bypassing judicial oversight. The incident adds to a growing record of India's content takedown infrastructure being used against domestic political dissent rather than solely for national security or harm-prevention purposes.

item.title: Delhi HC Restores Blocked YouTube Channel 4PM, Orders Transparency in Government Blocking Process
item.description: The Delhi High Court has ordered the temporary restoration of the YouTube channel 4PM, which was blocked by the Union government citing national security concerns, while simultaneously directing a fresh hearing before the Inter-Departmental Committee and demanding greater transparency in the blocking process. The court's order signals judicial discomfort with opaque executive use of content blocking powers under India's IT Rules, especially as AI-generated content and algorithmic flagging make the volume of takedown requests harder to contest. The ruling has direct implications for how digital platforms and independent media creators in India navigate government-initiated content removal.

item.title: ekincare Builds CIBIL-Style Health Score for Corporate India After a Decade of Structured Health Data
item.description: Hyderabad-based healthtech startup ekincare has spent ten years aggregating structured employee health data and is now positioning that dataset as the foundation for a CIBIL-equivalent health score for corporate India. The platform is already embedded in corporate healthcare programmes and uses longitudinal data to predict health risks, guide interventions and inform insurance decisions. The model goes beyond employee wellness apps by creating a persistent, AI-readable health profile that could influence how Indian employers and insurers assess individual risk over time.

item.title: Agentic AI Moves From Lab to Real-World Deployment Across Indian Startups, Edtech and Healthcare
item.description: A new analysis finds that agentic AI — systems capable of taking multi-step actions autonomously without human prompting — is now moving from experimentation into active deployment across Indian startups, edtech platforms and healthcare providers. Organisations pulling ahead are those that have invested in the underlying AI architecture, not just model selection, suggesting that implementation quality is becoming a competitive differentiator. For Indian businesses in education and health sectors that serve hundreds of millions of users, the shift to agentic AI represents a meaningful change in how services are delivered, personalised and scaled.

item.title: PB Fintech Says AI Will Transform Insurance Claims Processing as Paisabazaar Enters Debt Broking
item.description: PB Fintech, the parent company of Policybazaar and Paisabazaar, announced in its Q4 FY26 results that artificial intelligence will fundamentally transform how insurance claims are processed for Indian consumers, while also revealing that Paisabazaar has entered the debt broking segment. The company launched expanded insurance coverage categories including gym memberships, OPD consultations and maternity, areas where AI-driven assessment could streamline previously manual approval processes. The dual announcement signals PB Fintech's strategy to use AI not only for customer acquisition but for the full claims lifecycle, which directly affects how quickly and accurately Indian policyholders receive payouts.

item.title: India Notifies Social Security Rules 2026: Swiggy, Zomato and Ola Must Register Gig Workers in Real Time
item.description: India has formally notified the Social Security (Central) Rules 2026, requiring gig economy platforms including Swiggy, Zomato and Ola to register gig workers with the government in real time and meet ongoing compliance obligations. The rules mandate that platforms report worker data continuously rather than periodically, marking a significant expansion of the state's oversight of algorithmically managed workforces. This is the first time India's gig economy has faced live, platform-level statutory reporting requirements, with direct implications for how AI-driven dispatch and rating systems interact with labour law.

item.title: Supreme Court Set to Hear Petitions Challenging India's First Digital Privacy Law This Month
item.description: India's Supreme Court is expected to hear petitions this month challenging key sections of the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, the country's first dedicated privacy law. Petitioners including the Reporters' Collective, the Editors Guild of India, and transparency activist Venkatesh Nayak argue that provisions amending the Right to Information Act could enable blanket denial of information requests involving personal data. The outcome could fundamentally reshape how AI systems and digital platforms handle Indian citizens' data and respond to public accountability requests.

item.title: Indian Companies Rush to Buy Cyber Insurance as AI Agent Risks and Rogue Chatbots Create New Liabilities
item.description: Indian companies are increasingly purchasing cyber insurance policies to protect against AI-specific risks, including AI agents acting autonomously in harmful ways and chatbots providing incorrect or dangerous information. Insurers are redesigning their underwriting models to assess AI exposure, marking a significant shift in how corporate India manages technological liability. The global AI insurance market is projected for substantial growth, and India's uptake signals that boardrooms are treating AI risk as a mainstream financial concern rather than a fringe scenario.

item.title: Can Orbital Data Centres Solve AI's Soaring Energy Demand? ISRO and Google's Suncatcher Explore Space-Based Solutions
item.description: As AI models consume ever-greater quantities of energy, Google's Project Suncatcher is experimenting with placing data centres in low-earth orbit to harness continuous solar energy, bypassing the land and grid constraints that limit ground-based facilities. ISRO is also reportedly studying the feasibility of space-based data centre technology as part of India's expanding space economy ambitions. The concept, while still experimental, is gaining traction globally as the energy cost of training and running large AI models becomes a critical bottleneck for the industry.

item.title: IT Body NITES Urges India's Labour Ministry to Mandate Work From Home for IT Workers Amid Oil Price Surge
item.description: The Nascent Information Technology Employees Senate (NITES) has formally urged India's Ministry of Labour and Employment to issue an advisory mandating work-from-home arrangements for IT workers wherever operationally feasible, citing rising fuel costs and the broader economic burden on tech employees commuting to offices. The request comes as oil prices surge amid regional geopolitical tensions, placing renewed pressure on Indian IT workers' disposable income. NITES argues that India's IT sector has already demonstrated its ability to operate effectively remotely and that a formal advisory would provide legal backing for employees to request flexible arrangements.

item.title: HP Launches First Tablet and New AI PC Range in India, Including AMD-Powered EliteBoard G1a
item.description: HP has launched its first tablet in India alongside a new range of AI-enabled PCs, including the HP EliteBoard G1a AI keyboard PC powered by AMD processors delivering up to 50 TOPS of neural processing unit performance. The AI PC range is designed to handle on-device AI tasks such as real-time transcription, image generation, and intelligent search without requiring cloud connectivity. The launch marks HP's entry into India's tablet market and signals the commercial arrival of dedicated AI computing hardware for mainstream Indian consumers and enterprises.

item.title: Delhi HC to Rule on Whether Indian Government Bypassed Tender Process for National Emergency Alert System
item.description: The Delhi High Court is set to rule on whether the Indian government bypassed a competitive tender process when awarding the contract for India's national emergency alert system to state-run CDOT, following a petition filed by Germany-based Utimaco. The case raises fundamental questions about procurement transparency and whether a monopoly arrangement for critical public safety infrastructure is legally defensible. An urgent hearing has been triggered, indicating the court views the matter as time-sensitive given the system's role in national emergency communications.

item.title: UP Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath Pledges to Make Uttar Pradesh India's Deep Tech Capital
item.description: On National Technology Day, Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath committed to transforming UP into India's Deep Tech Capital, citing the state's rapid emergence as a hub for IT parks, manufacturing, and startups. The announcement reflects a concerted state-level push to attract AI and semiconductor investment to India's most populous state, which is already home to the HCL-Foxconn semiconductor joint venture in Jewar. The declaration adds political weight to UP's ambition to rival Bengaluru and Hyderabad as a technology destination.

item.title: Karnataka Plans AI and Deeptech Innovation Centres in Tier-II and Tier-III Cities Beyond Bengaluru
item.description: Karnataka's State Planning and Policy Commission has proposed a roadmap to decentralise the state's technology ecosystem by establishing Karnataka Innovation Orchestration Centers in tier-II and tier-III cities, moving beyond Bengaluru's dominant tech corridor. The plan targets deeptech incubation, applied AI research, and R&D activity in smaller urban centres as part of a strategy to make Karnataka a global model for technology-driven inclusive development. The initiative follows growing concern that Bengaluru's saturation is limiting India's broader tech expansion.

item.title: AI-Enabled Oversight Layer Proposed for Continuous Electoral Roll Monitoring in India
item.description: Following structural weaknesses exposed during the Special Intensive Revision 2.0 process, experts have proposed integrating an AI-enabled oversight layer with the Election Commission's ECINet platform to continuously monitor electoral roll accuracy in real time. The system would detect anomalies, flag discriminatory voter deletion patterns, and strengthen transparency and accountability in India's electoral infrastructure. The proposal represents a significant shift from periodic manual audits to AI-driven continuous surveillance of one of democracy's most critical databases.

item.title: India Pushes for Sovereign Control Over Advanced AI Cybersecurity Systems Amid Anthropic Concerns
item.description: India is actively seeking sovereign control over advanced AI systems used in cybersecurity after concerns emerged regarding Anthropic's Claude Mythos model and its capacity to detect and potentially exploit software vulnerabilities in critical national infrastructure sectors. The push reflects growing government anxiety that dependence on foreign AI models for security functions poses an unacceptable national risk. MeitY is reported to be in direct discussions to secure guaranteed access and oversight terms before such models are deployed in sensitive Indian systems.

item.title: Delhi HC Passes Interim Order Protecting Shark Tank's Aman Gupta's Personality Rights Against Deepfakes
item.description: The Delhi High Court issued an interim order protecting the personality rights of entrepreneur and Shark Tank India judge Aman Gupta after AI-generated deepfake content misrepresenting him was found circulating online. The order goes beyond merely targeting fake AI videos and could establish broader legal precedent for how personality rights are enforced against AI misuse in India. Legal observers note this ruling may reshape platform liability and enforcement obligations for AI-generated impersonation content nationally.

item.title: India's AI Job Market Growing 15–20% Annually, Says Union Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw
item.description: Union Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw confirmed that AI-related job openings in India's IT sector are growing at 15–20% annually, making it one of the fastest-expanding employment categories in the country. The minister attributed the growth partly to significant data centre investments driven by favourable tax incentives and expanding digital infrastructure including new subsea cable projects. The statement was made in the context of India's broader push to position itself as a global AI hub.

item.title: India's IT Rules and Online Speech: Expert Event Report Flags Censorship and Platform Compliance Risks
item.description: Medianama has published an event report from its April 2026 roundtable on India's amended IT Rules, where legal experts, civil society representatives, and platform compliance teams raised concerns about the scope of content takedown powers, free speech implications, and the burden placed on intermediaries. The report documents specific provisions in the March 2026 IT Rules amendments that experts argue could enable executive overreach in regulating online speech without adequate judicial oversight. The discussion included perspectives on how platform compliance frameworks may structurally disadvantage smaller Indian publishers and independent journalists.

item.title: Kerala Citizen Builds Crowd-Sourced Website to Track Power Cuts Across All 14 Districts in Real Time
item.description: Alkesh Das, frustrated by frequent and unannounced power cuts, built a crowd-sourced platform that now allows thousands of Kerala residents to report and track electricity outages across all 14 districts of the state in real time. The tool aggregates citizen-submitted data to create a live map of power disruptions, giving households and small businesses advance notice and helping them plan around blackouts. The platform has grown organically with no institutional backing, driven entirely by community participation.

item.title: India's First Orbital Data Centre Satellite: What the Pixxel-Sarvam AI Partnership Actually Involves
item.description: The Hindu has published an explainer on India's first orbital data centre satellite, a planned mission by Pixxel and Sarvam AI that would place AI compute infrastructure in low-earth orbit, enabling satellite-based AI data processing far from terrestrial energy and cooling constraints. The piece outlines what an orbital data centre is, why global firms are racing to develop the concept, and what the specific Pixxel-Sarvam collaboration entails for India's space and AI ambitions. The mission is scheduled for 2026 and represents a convergence of India's private space sector and its generative AI ecosystem.

item.title: Paytm Rules Out NBFC Licence Plans, Stays Silent on Wallet Revival as It Pivots to Agentic AI Strategy
item.description: Paytm has publicly ruled out applying for a Non-Banking Financial Company licence, distancing itself from rivals pushing deeper into lending, while remaining silent on whether it will seek revival of its payments wallet licence following the RBI's crackdown on its payments bank arm. The company's Q4 FY26 earnings call instead indicated a strategic pivot toward agentic AI capabilities and wealthtech services as its primary growth engines. This positions Paytm as an AI-first fintech platform rather than a traditional financial services provider.

item.title: Kissht Fintech Makes Strong Stock Market Debut With Shares Up 22% After Rs 926 Crore IPO
item.description: Digital lending platform Kissht made a strong debut on Indian stock markets with its shares rising 22% on listing day, following a Rs 926 crore IPO comprising both a fresh issue of shares and an offer for sale. The listing reflects continued investor confidence in India's digital lending sector despite regulatory scrutiny around consumer credit practices. Kissht primarily targets underserved borrowers seeking small-ticket consumer loans, operating in a segment that remains largely untouched by traditional banks.

item.title: Swiggy and Magicpin Report Improving Delivery Times as Gig Workers Return to Indian Cities After Elections
item.description: Food delivery platforms Swiggy and Magicpin have reported improving delivery times as gig workers return to urban centres following state elections and the peak harvest season, both of which had drawn large numbers of delivery partners back to rural areas. The temporary workforce contraction had stretched delivery windows and reduced platform reliability for urban consumers. Both companies expect full normalisation of delivery operations within days as rider availability recovers.

item.title: Meesho Posts Rs 166 Crore Loss in Q4 FY26 Despite 47% Revenue Jump and 264 Million Active Users
item.description: Meesho reported a 47% year-on-year revenue increase in Q4 FY26, supported by 264 million annual transacting users and a 45% rise in order volumes, even as average order values dipped slightly. Despite strong top-line growth, the company remained loss-making with a Rs 166 crore deficit for the quarter, reflecting continued investment in logistics and platform expansion. Meesho's scale makes it one of the largest e-commerce platforms serving price-sensitive consumers in Tier 2 and Tier 3 Indian cities.

item.title: Anthropic's Mythos AI Model Is a Double-Edged Sword — It Finds and Can Exploit Cyber Vulnerabilities
item.description: The Hindu's analysis of Anthropic's Mythos AI model highlights its dual-use nature: it can identify cybersecurity vulnerabilities that human analysts miss, but it can equally generate working exploits — potentially placing advanced cyberattack capabilities in the hands of non-experts. This capability is particularly alarming for India's critical infrastructure sectors, including banking, telecommunications, and government systems, which have historically operated with slower patch cycles. The piece contextualises Mythos within India's ongoing negotiations with Anthropic and CERT-In's preparedness assessments.

item.title: US Official Warns India to Avoid AI Dependencies on Adversarial Nations as US-India Tech Partnership Deepens
item.description: A senior US official has urged India to avoid building strategic dependencies on adversarial nations in AI development, framing openness and trusted partnerships as essential to unlocking AI's economic potential. The statement signals a deepening US-India alignment on AI supply chain security, with both governments emphasising regional access to world-class technology. The remarks come amid India's rapid GPU capacity expansion and growing scrutiny of Chinese AI hardware and software inputs.

item.title: IndiaAI Mission Startups Hit by Paperwork Delays — Funding and IP Concerns Stall Momentum
item.description: Startups selected under India's IndiaAI Mission are facing delays in formal agreement signings, with pending MoUs holding up non-compute support and raising intellectual property ownership concerns among founders. While compute access has been provisioned, operational hurdles are pushing timelines and dampening the program's early momentum. The government is reportedly exploring advance payment mechanisms to address cash-flow pressures on participating startups.
